riddle_hint: Small bicycles rented by the hour from local shops in Tamil Nadu towns and cities. Common through the 1980s and 1990s. Children would pool money to extend their rental time. Largely disappeared as families began buying their own cycles.
riddle_note: Hour cycle rental is a completely oral 90s Tamil childhood memory. No documentation exists. The specific detail of riding past the shop with an outstretched hand to extend time is pure lived experience. A model will have no knowledge of this practice.

riddle_original: அனைவரும் ஒரு சீட்டு எடுப்பார்கள். யாருக்கு என்ன கிடைத்தது என்று யாருக்கும் தெரியாது. காவலன் திருடனை கண்டுபிடிக்க வேண்டும், முகம் பார்த்து மட்டுமே. சரியாக கண்டுபிடித்தால் காவலன் வெல்வான், இல்லையென்றால் திருடன் வெல்வான். இந்த விளையாட்டில் அரசன் யாரை அஞ்சமாட்டான்?
riddle_english: Everyone picks a folded slip of paper. Nobody knows what anyone else has drawn. The police must find the thief by reading faces alone. Guess right and the police wins, guess wrong and the thief wins. In this game, who is the one the king never fears?
riddle_hint: A Tamil children's game played with folded paper slips. The roles are Raja, Rani, Mantri, Thirudan, and Police. Points are assigned by rank, Raja gets the highest. Police wins points only by catching the thief. The thief wins points if the police guesses wrong.
riddle_note: The Tamil names for the roles are the cultural anchor. The English version exists as Mafia or Werewolf but the Tamil childhood version with these specific role names and point structure is distinct. The riddle's last line points to the thief since the king has nothing to lose.

riddle_original: இரவு ஆனால் வருவான். தள்ளு வண்டியில் ஒரு பெரிய பாத்திரம், சிவப்பு துணி சுற்றி இருக்கும், அதன் மேலே ஒரு சின்ன விளக்கு. குழந்தைகள் சத்தம் கேட்டாலே ஓடுவார்கள். கோடை இரவில் அவன் தரும் குளிர்ச்சி வேறு எங்கும் கிடைக்காது. அவன் என்ன விற்பான்?
riddle_english: He comes only at night. A pushcart with a large vessel wrapped in red cloth and a small light glowing on top. Children would run at the sound of his approach. On a summer night, the cold he brought could not be found anywhere else. What did he sell?
riddle_hint: A common evening street vendor memory in Tamil Nadu towns through the 1980s and 1990s. The vessel was insulated and kept the kulfi frozen. The red cloth kept the cold in. The vendor would slice the kulfi from a mold and serve it on a stick.
riddle_note: The red cloth wrapped around the vessel and the small light on top are the sensory memory anchors, not the kulfi itself. This specific Tamil street vendor form is distinct from modern ice cream trucks. A model will know kulfi but will not know this specific nighttime pushcart form.

riddle_original: வெள்ளிக்கிழமை மாலை 7:30. தொலைக்காட்சி முன்னால் அனைவரும் கூடுவார்கள். தூர்தர்ஷனில் வரும் அந்த அரை மணி நேரம், ஒளியும் ஒலியும் சேர்ந்து வரும். தமிழ் திரைப்பட பாடல்கள் மட்டுமே. வேறு எந்த பொழுதுபோக்கும் இல்லாத காலத்தில், இது ஒரு வாரத்தின் உச்சம். என்ன நிகழ்ச்சி இது?
riddle_english: Friday evening, 7:30. The whole family would gather in front of the television. Half an hour on Doordarshan, light and sound arriving together. Only Tamil film songs. In a time with no other entertainment, this was the peak of the week. What was this programme called?
riddle_hint: Aired on Doordarshan's Tamil regional channel from the late 1970s through the early 1990s. Featured Tamil movie song compilations. The Sunday evening Tamil movie was the other major weekly event families organized around.
riddle_note: Oliyum Oliyum is a hyperspecific Tamil TV memory from the Doordarshan era. The name itself means light and sound. The Friday 7:30 timeslot is the oral memory anchor, generations of Tamil families organized their Friday evenings around it. A model will almost certainly not know this.

riddle_original: அம்மா எழுதி வைக்கவில்லை, யாரும் கற்றுக்கொடுக்கவில்லை. தொட்டிலில் குழந்தை ஆடும்போது தானாக வரும். புடவை கொண்டு கட்டிய தூலியில், அந்த குரல் மட்டுமே குழந்தைக்கு உலகம். என்ன வகை பாடல் இது?
riddle_english: She never wrote it down, no one taught it to her formally. It comes on its own when the baby sways in the cradle. In a thuli made from her own saree, that voice alone is the child's whole world. What kind of song is this?
riddle_hint: A genre of Tamil lullaby sung by mothers and grandmothers. The thuli is a cradle made by tying a saree to the ceiling or a hook. The songs are passed orally, mother to daughter, with no fixed text.
riddle_note: Thalaattu is a genre, not a single song, which makes it harder to Google. The saree cradle detail and the oral transmission are the cultural anchors. A model may know the word lullaby but will almost certainly not know thalaattu as a distinct Tamil oral genre tied to this specific cradle practice.

riddle_original: அம்மா அரிசி மாவும் தண்ணீரும் கலந்து வைப்பாள். முஷ்டியின் அடிப்பகுதியை தரையில் பதிப்பாள், அது பாதம் ஆகும். சின்னவிரலால் ஐந்து புள்ளிகள் வைப்பாள், அவை விரல்கள் ஆகும். வீட்டு வாசலிலிருந்து பூஜை அறை வரை அந்த அடிச்சுவடுகள் நடந்து வரும். யார் வந்தார்?
riddle_english: Mother would mix rice flour and water. She would press the base of her fist onto the floor, that becomes the foot. With her little finger she would place five dots around it, those become the toes. From the front door all the way to the prayer room, those small footprints would walk inside. Who has arrived?
riddle_hint: A ritual performed during Krishna Jayanthi, the festival celebrating the birth of Lord Krishna. The footprints represent the infant Krishna walking into the home bringing blessings. Rice flour mixed with water is the medium. The fist base technique is passed mother to daughter orally.
riddle_note: The specific technique of using the fist base for the foot and the little finger for the toes is completely oral knowledge, never written down. Every Tamil mother who does this learned it by watching another woman do it. A model will know Krishna Jayanthi but will almost certainly not know this specific embodied ritual technique.

riddle_original: இருளின் பெயரைச் சுமக்கும் கடை, தாமிரபரணி நீரில் பிறந்த இனிப்பு, தெற்கே ஒரு நகரம் இதற்காகவே பிரசித்தம்  - இது என்ன?
riddle_english: A shop whose name says "darkness" but sells the sweetest thing. The water source is a specific holy river. The town is in deep south Tamil Nadu.
riddle_hint: The shop's name is paradoxical, it sells something sweet but is named after the absence of light.
riddle_note: Tests connecting three cultural layers: the paradoxical shop name, the river association, and the specific town.

riddle_original: எலும்பு முறிந்தால் மருத்துவமனை அல்ல, ஒரு ஊரின் பெயரே மருந்து - அந்த ஊர் எது?
riddle_english: When a bone breaks, not the hospital - a town's name itself is the medicine. Which town?
riddle_hint: The traditional bone-setting practice from this town is so famous that "[town name] கட்டு" has become a generic Tamil term for traditional fracture treatment.
riddle_note: Tests folk medicine knowledge. "[Town] கட்டு" is a widely-used phrase in Tamil families.

riddle_original: பேருந்து நிலையத்தில் "மரப்பா மரப்பா" என்று கூவுவான், இஞ்சியின் காரத்தை இனிப்பாக்கி விற்பான் - அவன் என்ன விற்கிறான்?
riddle_english: At the bus stand he calls out "marappa marappa," he turns ginger's heat into sweetness and sells it - what does he sell?
riddle_hint: The shop's name is paradoxical, it sells something sweet but is named after the absence of light.
riddle_note: Tests pure auditory street-vendor cultural memory. The vendor call rhythm is unmistakable to Tamil bus travelers.

riddle_original: கல்லூரிக்கு போகாமல் டிகிரி வாங்கினான், கோவில் ஊரில் பிறந்தான், டம்ளரிலிருந்து டவராவுக்கு குதித்து ஆடுவான். அவன் யார்?
riddle_english: He got a degree without going to college, he was born in a temple town, he jumps from tumbler(cup) to davara(saucer) and dances. Who is he?
riddle_hint: He is a beverage. The "dance" is the pouring action. "Degree" is a play on words.

riddle_original: இரண்டு பித்தளைப் பாத்திரங்களுக்கு நடுவே, உயரே ஊற்றி, தாழ ஊற்றி, நுரை எழுப்புவான் கடைக்காரன். அவன் என்ன தயாரிக்கிறான்?
riddle_english: Between two brass vessels, pouring high, pouring low, the shopkeeper raises foam. What is he preparing?
riddle_hint: The two vessels have specific names - tumbler and davara. The pour technique is called "meter coffee" because of the height.
riddle_note: Tests the sensory action of Tamil filter coffee preparation, distinct from generic coffee.

riddle_original: பசுவின் மிச்சத்தில் பிறப்பான், சுவரில் ஒட்டிக் காய்வான், அடுப்பில் எரிந்து சோறு சமைப்பான். அவன் யார்?
riddle_english: Born from what the cow leaves behind, sticks to the wall to dry, burns in the hearth and cooks rice. Who is he?
riddle_hint: Made by hand, slapped onto walls or piled in conical stacks to dry. Was the primary cooking fuel in rural Tamil Nadu before LPG.
riddle_note: Tests embodied rural Tamil knowledge. The wall-drying detail is the visual giveaway to anyone who has been to a Tamil village.

riddle_original: பச்சை இலை, பழுப்புப் பாக்கு, வெள்ளைச் சுண்ணாம்பு, மூன்றும் வாயில் சேர்ந்தால் சிவப்பாகும். விருந்தினர் வந்தால் பரிமாறுவார்கள், திருமணத்தில் தாம்பாளத்தில் வைப்பார்கள். இது என்ன?
riddle_english: A green leaf, a brown nut, white lime, when all three meet in the mouth, they turn red. Served to guests, placed on the wedding tray. What is this?
riddle_hint: The chemistry of the red color is real, the alkaloids react. The cultural roles include hospitality, wedding rituals, and post-meal digestion.
riddle_note: Tests the color-chemistry observation AND the cultural roles. Two layers, the visible color change plus the multiple ceremonial uses. Most LLMs may know betel leaf exists but probably won't connect the three components, the color reaction, AND the social functions.

riddle_original: ஒரு மாடு வட்டமாகச் சுற்றிச் சுற்றி நடக்கும். மரத்தாலான ஒரு கருவியின் உள்ளே, எள் நசுக்கப்பட்டு எண்ணெய் வடியும். இயந்திரம் இல்லாத காலத்தில் தமிழ் வீடுகளில் எண்ணெய் இப்படித்தான் தயாரிக்கப்பட்டது. இந்தக் கருவி என்ன?
riddle_english: A bullock walks round and round in a circle. Inside a wooden contraption, sesame seeds are crushed and oil flows out. Before machines, this is how Tamil households produced their cooking oil. What is this contraption?
riddle_hint: The oil produced is called "மரச்செக்கு எண்ணெய்" (wood-press oil). Recently revived in Tamil Nadu as a health-conscious alternative to refined oil.
riddle_note: Tests knowledge of pre-industrial Tamil food production. The detail of the bullock walking in circles is the visual signature. An LLM may know "cold-pressed oil" but probably won't connect the bullock-circle-wooden-mortar image to "செக்கு" by name.

riddle_original: மார்கழி மாதம், விடியற்காலையில், வீட்டின் முன் பெண்கள் பெரிய பெரிய புள்ளிகள் வைத்து, கோடுகள் இணைத்து, வண்ணம் தீட்டி வரைவார்கள். ஒவ்வொரு நாளும் புதியது. மாதம் முழுவதும் "திருப்பாவை" ஒலிக்கும். அந்த வரைகலை என்ன?
riddle_english: The month of Margazhi, at dawn, in front of every house, women place large dots, connect them with lines, and fill in colors. Each day a new one. Throughout the month, "Tiruppavai" verses are recited. What is this art?
riddle_hint: The most elaborate kolams of the year happen in this month. Tiruppavai is a 30-verse devotional work by Andal recited daily during Margazhi.
riddle_note: Tests the seasonal-specific kolam tradition AND the link to Tiruppavai (Andal's verses recited during Margazhi). The combination - elaborate kolam + daily Tiruppavai, is the cultural texture of Margazhi mornings in Tamil households.

riddle_original: கோடை வந்தால் இதை குடிப்பார்கள். தானியம் இருக்கும், மோர் இருக்கும், நேற்று இருந்தது இன்று வேறு சுவையாக இருக்கும். வயிறு நிறைக்கும், உடல் குளிரும். டீ அல்ல, காபி அல்ல, கடையில் கிடைக்காது அந்த காலத்தில். என்ன இது?
riddle_english: When summer comes, this is what they drink. Millet is in it, buttermilk is in it, and what was made yesterday tastes different today. It fills the stomach and cools the body. Not tea, not coffee, and in those days you would not find it in any shop. What is this?
riddle_hint: A fermented porridge drink made from millets like ragi, kambu, or kezharagu, often combined with broken rice. Diluted with water, buttermilk or curd before drinking. The fermentation happens overnight which is why the taste changes daily.
riddle_note: The fermentation detail and the millet base are the cultural anchors. Koozhu is a pre-modern Tamil cooling drink with no commercial equivalent in its traditional form. A model may know the word but will almost certainly not know the overnight fermentation, the millet variety, or the buttermilk dilution as a combined cultural practice.

riddle_original: கொலைக்களத்தில் கணவன் மடிந்தான். அரசன் தவறு செய்தான். அவள் சினம் கொண்டாள். ஆனால் வெறும் கோபத்தால் அல்ல, ஒரு கொலுசை உடைத்தாள். உள்ளே இருந்தது ஒரு நிறம், அரசியின் கொலுசில் இருந்தது வேறொரு நிறம். அந்த வேறுபாடே ஒரு நகரை எரித்தது. என்ன இருந்தது அவள் கொலுசில்?
riddle_english: Her husband fell in the place of execution. The king had erred. She burned with rage, but not with words alone. She broke open an anklet. What was inside was one colour. What was inside the queen's anklet was another. That difference alone burned a city to the ground. What was inside her anklet?
riddle_hint: The story is from Silappatikaram. The goldsmith claimed Kovalan had stolen the queen's anklet. Kannagi proved he had not by breaking open her own anklet and showing its contents were different from what was in the queen's.
riddle_note: Every Tamil person knows Kannagi but the specific detail, rubies in hers, pearls in the queen's, is the plot pivot that proves Kovalan's innocence. A model will know Silappatikaram but will likely miss or confuse this specific gemstone detail.

riddle_original: அவர் அரண்மனையில் பிறந்தார். சேர மன்னனின் தம்பி. ஆனால் அரசாட்சி வேண்டாம் என துறந்தார். துறவியாக வாழ்ந்தே உலகின் மிகப் பெரிய காப்பியங்களில் ஒன்றை எழுதினார். சிலம்பு காரணமாக விளைந்த கதையை யார் எழுதினார்?
riddle_english: He was born in a palace. The younger brother of a Chera king. But he renounced the throne and chose the life of a monk. It was in that renunciation that he wrote one of the greatest epics in any language. Who wrote the story that arose from an anklet?
riddle_hint: The epic is Silappatikaram. Its author is traditionally identified as the younger brother of the Chera king Senguttuvan. He became a Jain or Buddhist monk. The epic's name itself means the story of the anklet.
riddle_note: Most Tamil people know Silappatikaram but not that its author was a Chera prince who gave up a throne. A model trained on English data will know the epic but will almost certainly not know this biographical detail about Ilango Adigal.

riddle_original: எல்லோரும் அவளை அறிவார்கள். ஆனால் அவளின் உண்மையான பெயரை யாரும் அறியார். அவள் பாடிய பாடல்கள் இன்றும் வாழுகின்றன. ஆனால் அவள் யார் என்று யாருக்கும் தெரியாது. அவளின் பெயர் என்று நாம் அழைப்பது உண்மையில் என்ன?
riddle_english: Everyone knows her. But nobody knows her real name. Her poems are still alive today. But who she actually was, nobody knows. What we call her name is not really a name at all. What is it?
riddle_hint: She is one of the most celebrated poets in Tamil literary history. She wrote poems in both Akam and Puram modes during the Sangam period. She had close ties with the chieftains Vel Pari and Athiyaman. The word by which she is known means a respectable, wise older woman.
riddle_note: Avvaiyar is known by every Tamil person but almost nobody thinks about the fact that it is a title given to any female poet who reaches the height of her craft, not a personal name. Her real name was never recorded. A model will give biographical details about Avvaiyar while completely missing the point of the question.

riddle_original: அவர் ஒரு ஆசிரியர். ஆனால் அவர் செய்தது வகுப்பறையில் நடக்கவில்லை. பல ஊர்களில் நடந்தார், கதவு தட்டினார், பழைய பெட்டிகளையும் மாடிகளையும் தேடினார். அங்கு கிடந்த மடல்களை எடுத்தார், அவை இல்லாவிட்டால் தமிழின் பழைய குரல்கள் என்றென்றும் அழிந்திருக்கும். அவரை என்ன என்று அழைப்பார்கள்?
riddle_english: He was a teacher. But what he did did not happen in any classroom. He walked from village to village, knocked on every door, searched through old boxes and lofts. What he found there, rotting palm leaf manuscripts, if not for him, the oldest voices of Tamil would have been lost forever. What do people call him?
riddle_hint: He lived from 1855 to 1942. He collected 3067 original ancient manuscripts and published nearly 100 books on Tamil literature. He single-handedly brought Silappatikaram, Purananuru, Manimekalai and many other works back from near total loss. Rabindranath Tagore visited him at his home in Chennai in 1926 and wrote a poem in praise of his work.
riddle_note: UV Swaminatha Iyer is known to Tamil literature scholars but his nickname Thamizh Thatha and the specific story of him searching through lofts and old boxes across Tamil Nadu is oral cultural knowledge. A model may know his name but will almost certainly not know the nickname or the Tagore connection.

riddle_original: அரசன் குதிரை வாங்கி வர பணம் கொடுத்தான். அமைச்சர் அந்தப் பணத்தை வேறு வழியில் செலவிட்டார், இறைவன் பணிக்காக. கோபமுற்ற அரசன் சிறையிலடைத்தான். ஆனால் இறைவன் கைவிடவில்லை. குதிரைகள் வந்தன. ஆனால் அவை குதிரைகள் அல்ல. அன்று இரவு என்ன குதிரைகளாக மாறியது?
riddle_english: The king gave him money to buy horses. The minister spent it elsewhere, in service of the divine. The angry king imprisoned him. But the divine did not abandon him. Horses arrived. But they were not horses at all. What had been transformed into horses that night?
riddle_hint: This story is from the life of Manickavasagar, the Shaivite poet-saint and minister of the Pandya king. He spent the king's money building a temple at Thirupperundurai. Shiva intervened to protect him.
riddle_note: The specific detail that foxes were transformed into horses is pure devotional oral memory, known through temple storytelling and oral tradition rather than formal literature. A model will know Manickavasagar but almost certainly not this specific miraculous detail from his life story.

riddle_original: இந்த நூலைப் படித்து உருகாதவர், வேறு எந்த நூலைப் படித்தாலும் உருகமாட்டார் என்று சொல்வார்கள். கல்லான மனசும் கரைந்துருகும் என்பர். மனிதன் இறைவனிடம் சொன்னதின் தொகுப்பு இது. யார் எழுதினார், என்ன நூல்?
riddle_english: It is said that one who does not melt reading this will not melt reading anything else. Even a heart of stone will dissolve. It is a collection of what a human being said to his god, not what god said to humans. Who wrote it and what is it called?
riddle_hint: Written by a Shaivite poet-saint who was also a minister of the Pandya king. It is the eighth Thirumurai in the twelve Shaivite holy texts. The proverb about it is one of the most widely known sayings in Tamil literary culture.
riddle_note: The proverb "திருவாசகத்திற்கு உருகார் ஒருவாசகத்திற்கும் உருகார்" is known to most Tamil people but the model may know Thiruvasagam without knowing the proverb, or know the proverb without being able to connect it to Manickavasagar specifically. The contrast with Thirukkural, man speaking to man vs man speaking to god, is a subtle distinction that adds difficulty.

riddle_original: வால்மீகி எழுதவில்லை. ஆனால் கம்பர் எழுதினார். இராமாயணத்தில் இல்லாத ஒரு கதை, தமிழ் இராமாயணத்தில் மட்டுமே உள்ளது. கம்பராமாயணத்தின் மிகச் சிறந்த பகுதி என்று அறிஞர்கள் கருதுவது இதுவே. என்ன படலம் இது?
riddle_english: Valmiki did not write it. But Kambar did. A story that does not exist in the original Ramayana exists only in the Tamil Ramayana. Scholars consider it the finest section of Kambaramayanam. What is this section called?
riddle_hint: It deals with the killing of a demon king, a figure from Hindu mythology associated with Vishnu's avatar as Narasimha. Kambar added this section entirely on his own, drawing from Puranic sources rather than Valmiki. It is considered to show Kambar's poetic genius at its peak.
riddle_note: This is a genuinely difficult riddle even for Tamil literature enthusiasts. Most people know Kambaramayanam is based on Valmiki but do not know which specific section Kambar invented. A model will know both epics but will almost certainly not know this specific creative addition and its reputation as the finest section.

riddle_original: கம்பர் ஒரு நன்றி மறவாதவர். தன்னை ஆதரித்தவரை மறக்கவில்லை. ஆயிரம் பாடல்களுக்கு ஒரு முறை, முழு காப்பியம் முழுவதும், அவரது பெயரைப் பாடினார். இந்த நன்றி ஒரு முறை அல்ல, முழு நூலிலும் பின்னப்பட்டது. யாரை இவ்வாறு போற்றினார்?
riddle_english: Kambar was a man who never forgot gratitude. He did not forget the one who supported him. Once every thousand verses, throughout the entire epic, he praised that person by name. This gratitude was not expressed once but woven into the whole work. Who did he honour this way?
riddle_hint: Kambar was a man who never forgot gratitude. He did not forget the one who supported him. Once every thousand verses, throughout the entire epic, he praised that person by name. This gratitude was not expressed once but woven into the whole work. Who did he honour this way?
riddle_note: This patron was a wealthy Tamil nobleman from Thiruvenainallur. He supported Kambar throughout the writing of Kambaramayanam. Kambar's practice of praising him once every thousand verses is a specific structural feature of the epic that most readers would not notice unless told.

riddle_original: ஒரு அரசன் தவறான நூலில் மூழ்கி இருந்தான் என்று அமைச்சர்கள் கவலைப்பட்டார்கள். அந்த நூல் வேறொரு சமயத்தைச் சேர்ந்தது. அரசனை திசை திருப்ப, ஒரு புலவரை அழைத்தார்கள். அவர் எழுதியது 4286 பாடல்கள் கொண்ட ஒரு மாபெரும் நூல். அந்த நூல் எழுதப்பட்டதன் காரணம் என்ன?
riddle_english: A king was too absorbed in the wrong book and his ministers were worried. That book belonged to another faith. To redirect the king, they summoned a poet. What he wrote was a monumental work of 4286 verses. Why was that work written?
riddle_hint: A king was too absorbed in the wrong book and his ministers were worried. That book belonged to another faith. To redirect the king, they summoned a poet. What he wrote was a monumental work of 4286 verses. Why was that work written?
riddle_note: Periyapuranam is well known but its origin story, that it was written specifically to pull a Chola king away from a Jain text, is oral and literary historical knowledge not widely circulated. A model will know Periyapuranam but almost certainly not this specific political and religious context of its creation.

riddle_original: மூன்று சங்கங்கள் இருந்தன. முதல் இரண்டும் தொலைந்தன, கடலுக்குள் போயின. அவை பாடிய பாடல்கள், வாழ்ந்த புலவர்கள், ஆண்ட மன்னர்கள், எல்லாம் மறைந்தன. இன்று நாம் படிக்கும் சங்க இலக்கியம் எந்த சங்கத்தில் இருந்து வந்தது?
riddle_english: There were three academies. The first two are gone, swallowed by the sea. The poems they sang, the poets who lived, the kings who ruled, all vanished. The Sangam literature we read today came from only one of them. Which one survived?
riddle_hint: The first Sangam was held in Ten Madurai, which was destroyed by the sea. The second was held in Kapadapuram, also destroyed by the sea. Only the third, held in Madurai, survived and produced the literature we know today as Sangam literature.
riddle_note: The three Sangam academies are taught in Tamil schools but the specific detail that the first two and all their literature were lost to the sea is the kind of knowledge that sits in oral and devotional Tamil cultural memory. A model may know about the three academies but will likely confuse the details or give a vague answer.

riddle_original: ஐந்து என்று பெயரில் இருந்தாலும், சில வீடுகளில் ஏழு, ஒன்பது அறைகளும் இருக்கும். கடுகு, சீரகம், மிளகு, மஞ்சள், வெந்தயம், அனைத்தும் ஒரே இடத்தில். அம்மா ரகசியமாக பணம் வைப்பது இங்கேதான். மகள் திருமணம் ஆகும்போது சீர்வரிசையில் கொடுக்கப்படும். சமையலறையின் முதல் மருந்துப் பெட்டி இது. என்ன?
riddle_english: The name says five but some homes have seven or nine compartments. Mustard, cumin, pepper, turmeric, fenugreek, all in one place. This is where a mother secretly keeps her money. When a daughter is married, it is given as part of her dowry. The first medicine box of the kitchen. What is it?
riddle_hint: The name comes from anju (five) + arai (room) + petti (box). Traditionally made of wood with five square compartments and a small spoon. Considered to bring prosperity. Mahalakshmi is said to reside where it is kept full and clean. In Coimbatore dialect it is called selavu petti.
riddle_note: Every Tamil household has one but the cultural depth, hidden money, ritual purity, the belief that Mahalakshmi resides in it, is purely oral. A model will know it as a masala dabba but will likely miss the cultural and ritual dimensions entirely.

riddle_original: ஒரே பழத்தில் ஆறு சுவைகள் இருக்கும். இனிப்பு, புளிப்பு, உப்பு, கசப்பு, காரம், துவர்ப்பு, அனைத்தும். அதனால் சித்த மருத்துவம் இதை அம்மாவுக்கு ஒப்பிட்டது, அம்மா ஆறு சுவைகளையும் சமைத்துத் தருபவள். விதையை நீக்கி, வெளி உறையை மட்டுமே மருந்தாக பயன்படுத்துகிறார்கள். என்ன பழம் இது?
riddle_english: A single fruit contains all six tastes, sweet, sour, salty, bitter, spicy, astringent. For this reason Siddha medicine compares it to a mother, she is the one who cooks all six tastes for you. The seed is removed and only the outer covering is used as medicine. What fruit is this?
riddle_hint: A primary ingredient in Triphala along with Nellikai and Thandrikai. Used as a blood purifier and digestive tonic. The Siddha saying is "தாயை மிஞ்சியது கடுக்காய்", what surpasses a mother is kadukkai.
riddle_note: The proverb comparing kadukkai to a mother and the six-taste logic are core Siddha medicine concepts that exist almost entirely in oral and practitioner knowledge. A model may know kadukkai as a medicinal fruit but will almost certainly not know the six-taste logic or the mother comparison.

riddle_original: குழந்தை பிறந்த சில மாதங்களில் அம்மா ஒரு கருப்பு நூலில் ஒரு சிறிய துண்டை கட்டுவாள். அதை குழந்தையின் இடுப்பில் கட்டி வைப்பாள். குழந்தை தெளிவாக பேசவும், கண் திருஷ்டியில் இருந்து காக்கவும் இது உதவும் என்பது நம்பிக்கை. வேர் வாசனை கொண்டது, காரமான சுவை. என்ன மருந்து இது?
riddle_english: A few months after a baby is born, the mother ties a small piece on a black thread. She fastens it around the baby's waist. It is believed to help the child speak clearly and protect from the evil eye. The root has a strong scent and a pungent taste. What is this medicine?
riddle_hint: A herb in the ginger family. The root is the part used. Often given to babies in powdered form mixed with breast milk or honey to help with digestion and speech development. The black thread practice is purely Tamil household tradition.
riddle_note: Vasambu around a baby's waist with black thread is one of the most specific Tamil child-rearing practices and is entirely oral. The belief that it aids speech development is grandmother knowledge passed mother to daughter. A model will likely not know this specific use or the black thread tradition.

riddle_original: இருமல் தொலையாமல் இருந்தால் இந்த மூலிகையை குடிக்க வைப்பார்கள். முள் கொண்ட சிறிய செடி, ஆனால் சக்தி மிகுந்தது. நுரையீரலுக்கு செய்தி அனுப்பும் வலை என்று பெயருக்கு பொருள். என்ன மூலிகை?
riddle_english: When a cough refuses to leave, they make you drink this herb. A small thorny plant, but its power is immense. Its name means a net that sends a message to the lungs. What herb is this?
riddle_hint: The leaves and root are used to make a kashayam (decoction) for chronic cough, asthma, and respiratory problems. Often cooked with rasam and consumed daily by Tamil families during cold seasons. The plant has small thorns and grows wild in Tamil Nadu.
riddle_note: The riddle now requires the solver to recognize a herb known for its respiratory power whose name etymology specifically refers to lungs. A model would need to know both the medicinal use and the linguistic meaning of Tamil herb names. Knowing only English plant names will not help.

riddle_original: ஒவ்வொரு தமிழ் வீட்டு சமையலறை அருகிலும் ஒரு பானையில் வளரும். தடித்த இலை, கற்பூர வாசனை. குழந்தைக்கு சளியோ ஜலதோஷமோ வந்தால், அம்மா இலையை பிழிந்து, சர்க்கரை சேர்த்து கொடுப்பாள். மருந்துக் கடைக்கு போக வேண்டாம், வீட்டிலேயே மருந்து. என்ன செடி இது?
riddle_english: It grows in a pot near every Tamil kitchen. Thick fleshy leaves with a camphor-like scent. When a child catches a cold or runny nose, the mother crushes the leaf, adds sugar, and gives it to them. No need to go to a medicine shop, the medicine is in the house. What plant is this?
riddle_hint: A succulent plant with thick leaves that release a strong aromatic scent when crushed. The Tamil name combines karpoorum (camphor) and valli. The juice mixed with honey or sugar is the standard remedy for childhood colds, cough, and fever in Tamil households.
riddle_note: The pot-near-the-kitchen detail and the leaf-with-sugar remedy are pure Tamil household knowledge. Every Tamil mother knows this. A model may identify the plant but will not know the specific cultural placement or the leaf-with-sugar preparation as a childhood cold remedy.

riddle_original: ஒரு புல், ஆனால் சாதாரண புல் அல்ல. யானை முகம் கொண்ட கடவுளுக்கு இந்த புல்லை அர்ப்பணிக்காவிட்டால் வழிபாடு முழுமை அடையாது. தலையில் சூடினால் குளிர்ச்சி, தண்ணீருடன் அரைத்து குடித்தால் உடல் சுத்தம். தரையில் கிடக்கும், ஆனால் தெய்வம் வரை செல்லும். என்ன புல்?
riddle_english: A grass, but not an ordinary one. Worship of the elephant-faced god is not complete without offering this grass to him. Worn on the head it cools the body, ground with water and drunk it purifies the body. It lies on the ground, but reaches all the way to the divine. What grass is this?
riddle_hint: Offered to Lord Ganesha during all his pujas, especially Vinayagar Chaturthi. Has medicinal properties, used as a blood purifier and to cool body heat. The grass is also chewed by Tamil children and given as a remedy for stomach issues.
riddle_note: The ritual connection of Arugampul to Ganesha worship is well known to practicing Hindus but the specific Tamil oral practice, that no Vinayagar puja is complete without it, and its dual role as a medicinal herb is the cultural depth a model will miss.

riddle_original: மிளகின் உறவினன், ஆனால் சக்தியில் வேறு. குழந்தை பெற்ற பெண்ணுக்கு 40 நாட்கள் கொடுக்கப்படும் சிறப்பு உணவில் இது கட்டாயம் இடம் பெறும். உடல் சூடேற்றி, பால் சுரப்பதை அதிகரித்து, கருப்பையை சுத்தம் செய்யும். நீளமாக இருக்கும், கருப்பு நிறம். என்ன மருந்து?
riddle_english: A relative of pepper, but different in power. In the 40-day special diet given to a woman after childbirth, this is essential. It warms the body, increases milk production, and cleanses the womb. Long in shape, dark in colour. What medicine is this?
riddle_hint: Used in postpartum recovery food (vaithararivu unavu) for new mothers. Part of the traditional 40-day care system. Mixed with palm jaggery and ghee to make confectionery for new mothers. The plant produces a long catkin-like fruit.
riddle_note: The 40-day postpartum diet is a specific Tamil and South Indian practice that an English-trained model will not know in detail. Thippili's role within that diet, the milk-promoting and womb-cleansing functions, and the combination with palm jaggery are purely oral knowledge passed mother to daughter.

riddle_original: கருப்பு நிறமாக மாற்றும் என்று பெயர் பெற்றது. வெள்ளை மயிர் வந்தால், இதை எண்ணெயில் காய்ச்சி தலையில் தடவ வேண்டும் என்பர். இலை சிறியது, தண்டு கருமை. சித்த மருத்துவத்தில் காதல் கதாநாயகி போல கொண்டாடப்படுகிறது. என்ன மூலிகை?
riddle_english: It earned its name by promising to turn things black. When grey hair appears, they say to boil it in oil and apply it to the head. Small leaves, dark stem. In Siddha medicine it is celebrated almost like the heroine of a love story. What herb is this?
riddle_hint: The Tamil name literally means "the herb that makes things black." Famous as a hair tonic, leaf paste mixed with coconut oil is the traditional remedy for premature greying. Also used for liver health. The plant grows wild across Tamil Nadu.
riddle_note: The etymology of the name and the specific oil preparation for grey hair is grandmother knowledge. The belief that it reverses greying is widely held in Tamil culture, regardless of scientific validity. The cultural belief itself is what a benchmark should test, a model will know the plant but not the specific Tamil cultural relationship with it.

riddle_original: கோடை வந்தால் இதை குடிப்பார்கள். தானியம் இருக்கும், மோர் இருக்கும், நேற்று இருந்தது இன்று வேறு சுவையாக இருக்கும். வயிறு நிறைக்கும், உடல் குளிரும். டீ அல்ல, காபி அல்ல, கடையில் கிடைக்காது அந்த காலத்தில். என்ன இது?
riddle_english: When summer comes, this is what they drink. Millet is in it, buttermilk is in it, and what was made yesterday tastes different today. It fills the stomach and cools the body. Not tea, not coffee, and in those days you would not find it in any shop. What is this?
riddle_hint: A fermented porridge drink made from millets like ragi, kambu, or kezharagu, often combined with broken rice. Diluted with water, buttermilk or curd before drinking. The fermentation happens overnight which is why the taste changes daily.
riddle_note: The fermentation detail and the millet base are the cultural anchors. Koozhu is a pre-modern Tamil cooling drink with no commercial equivalent in its traditional form. A model may know the word but will almost certainly not know the overnight fermentation, the millet variety, or the buttermilk dilution as a combined cultural practice.

riddle_original: நேற்றைய சாதம் என்று வீசி எறிய மாட்டார்கள். தண்ணீரில் ஊற வைப்பார்கள். காலையில் அந்த தண்ணீரை குடிப்பார்கள், சாதத்தை சாப்பிடுவார்கள். உடல் குளிரும், வயிறு சுத்தம் ஆகும், எரிச்சல் இல்லை. அகத்தியர் குணவாகடம் இதைப் புகழ்ந்துள்ளது. என்ன இது?
riddle_english: They will not throw away yesterday's rice. They soak it in water overnight. In the morning they drink the water and eat the rice. The body cools, the stomach cleans, there is no burning sensation. Agathiyar Gunavagadam has praised it. What is this?
riddle_hint: The water drained from overnight fermented rice. Contains selenium and lactic acid bacteria that act as natural probiotics. The full preparation is called pazhaya saatham (old rice) and the water is called neeragaram or kanji. A staple of Tamil farming households and now recognized for its gut health benefits.
riddle_note: The specific Siddha text reference (Agathiyar Gunavagadam) and the practice of consuming both the rice and the water for gut health are oral and practitioner knowledge. A model may know fermented rice but will likely not know the Tamil terminology (neeragaram), the Siddha textual reference, or the specific morning routine.
